WI-01_Password_Reset_and_Account_Lockout.title: WI-01 Password Reset and Account Lockout
WI-01_Password_Reset_and_Account_Lockout.summary: Use this instruction when a user cannot sign in because of a forgotten or expired password, a locked account, or a failed multi-factor authentication (MFA) prompt. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if a VIP or a business-critical role) Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 30 min Handled by: Tier 1 Related: WI-10 Security Incidents, WI-11 Mobile Devices, WI-09 Access Requests

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: "Incorrect password" or "Account locked" message at sign-in
Password expired and the change prompt fails
MFA code not received, or authenticator app lost or replaced
Repeated prompts to sign in to Microsoft 365 or other apps

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Full name, username, and employee ID
Which system or application shows the error, and the exact message
Device in use and whether it is on the corporate network or remote
When the problem started, and whether the password was changed recently

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Verify identity. Confirm the caller using at least two items from the approved verification list (employee ID, manager name, date of birth on file, callback to the registered number). Never reset on the strength of an email request alone.
2 Check account status. Open the directory console (Active Directory or Entra ID). Check if the account is locked, disabled, expired, or flagged for risky sign-in.
3 Find the lockout source. If the account is locked, review the lockout source (stale mobile mail profile, mapped drive, saved credential, scheduled task) so it does not lock again.
4 Unlock or reset. Unlock the account, or use the self-service reset portal where possible. If you must reset, set a temporary password and require a change at next sign-in.
5 Deliver credentials safely. Give the temporary password by phone or to the registered mobile number. Never put passwords in the ticket, chat, or email.
6 Handle MFA issues. For a lost or replaced phone, verify identity, remove the old authentication method, and guide the user to re-register. Issue a temporary access pass if policy allows.
7 Confirm sign-in works. Stay with the user until sign-in succeeds on the device and on one cloud application. Ask them to update saved passwords on phones and mapped drives.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Account shows signs of compromise (impossible-travel alerts, unknown devices, forwarding rules): raise a security incident (see WI-10)
Account is disabled by HR or Security and you did not disable it
Directory sync errors, or the reset fails with a system error

WI-02_New_User_Onboarding_and_Account_Se.title: WI-02 New User Onboarding and Account Setup
WI-02_New_User_Onboarding_and_Account_Se.summary: Use this instruction for a new employee, contractor, or intern request raised by HR or a hiring manager. All new-hire requests must be approved before work starts. Priority: P3 Medium (set due date to the start date) Response target: Ready 1 business day before start date Handled by: Tier 2 Related: WI-09 Access Requests, WI-17 Offboarding, WI-18 Asset Management
topics: New User Onboarding and Account Setup

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Onboarding request form submitted by HR
Manager requests equipment and access for an upcoming start date

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Full legal name, preferred name, job title, department, and manager
Start date, work location, and employment type (staff, contractor, intern)
Required applications, shared folders, and groups (use the role template if one exists)
Hardware needs (laptop, monitor, phone, headset) and any special requirements

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Validate the request. Confirm the HR approval and manager sign-off are attached. Check the start date and that no duplicate account exists.
2 Create the identity. Create the user in the directory using the naming standard. Set the manager, department, job title, and location attributes.
3 Assign licences and mailbox. Assign the licence bundle for the role. Confirm the mailbox is created and added to the correct distribution lists and teams.
4 Apply role-based access. Add the user to the security groups defined for the role template. Anything outside the template needs separate data-owner approval (see WI-09).
5 Prepare the device. Image the laptop, enrol it in device management, apply encryption, and install the standard software. Record the asset tag and serial number.
6 Set up MFA and credentials. Generate a temporary password and share it with the manager by an approved secure method. Schedule MFA enrolment for the first day.
7 Hand over and verify. On day one, confirm the user can sign in, send email, reach the VPN and key applications, and print. Walk through the self-service portal and how to raise tickets.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Approvals are missing or unclear, or access requested conflicts with segregation-of-duties rules
Hardware is not available in time for the start date
Role template does not exist or is out of date

WI-03_Laptop_Desktop_and_Peripheral_Issu.title: WI-03 Laptop, Desktop and Peripheral Issues
WI-03_Laptop_Desktop_and_Peripheral_Issu.summary: Use this instruction for hardware faults and performance problems on company-issued computers and their peripherals. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if user cannot work at all) Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 4 business hours Handled by: Tier 1, then Tier 2 / deskside Related: WI-18 Asset Management, WI-19 OS Updates and Patching, WI-10 Security Incidents

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Device will not power on, boots to a black screen, or restarts unexpectedly
Very slow performance, freezing, or overheating
Keyboard, mouse, webcam, headset, or docking station not working
Blue screen errors, disk full warnings, or battery not charging

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Asset tag or hostname, make and model
Exact symptoms, error text, and when it started
Any recent changes (updates, new software, drops or spills)
Whether the problem follows the user to another device or dock

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the basics. Confirm the charger is connected and the outlet works, cables are firm, and the device is not in sleep or airplane mode. Hold the power button for 15 seconds, then try again.
2 Isolate the fault. Disconnect all peripherals and test with a known-good charger, dock, or mouse. This separates a peripheral problem from a device problem.
3 Review system health. Remotely check CPU, memory, and disk usage, pending updates, uptime, and event logs. Restart if uptime is over 7 days.
4 Clear common causes. Free disk space, remove unneeded start-up items, run the manufacturer diagnostics, and install pending operating system and driver updates.
5 Back up user data. Before any repair or rebuild, confirm user data is synced to cloud storage or backed up. Do not reimage without confirmation from the user.
6 Repair or replace. If hardware has failed, log a warranty claim with the vendor or issue a loaner device from stock. Record the serial numbers of both devices.
7 Verify with the user. Confirm the user can sign in and open their key applications. Collect any returned faulty hardware and update the asset register.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Suspected physical damage, liquid exposure, or battery swelling (tell the user to power off and stop charging)
Repeated crashes after a rebuild, suggesting a hardware fault
Lost or stolen device: raise a security incident immediately (see WI-10)

WI-04_Software_Installation_Updates_and_.title: WI-04 Software Installation, Updates and Licensing
WI-04_Software_Installation_Updates_and_.summary: Use this instruction when a user requests new software, cannot install or update an application, or reports a licensing error. Priority: P4 Low (P3 if blocking critical work) Response target: Respond in 30 min / resolve in 1 business day Handled by: Tier 1 / Tier 2 Related: WI-03 Laptops and Peripherals, WI-09 Access Requests, WI-20 Browser and Web Apps

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: User requests an application not on their device
Installation fails or is blocked by policy
"Unlicensed product" or "trial expired" message
Application crashes after an update

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Application name, version, and business reason
Hostname and operating system
Exact error message or screenshot
Manager approval for software that carries a cost

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the approved catalogue. Look in the software catalogue or company portal first. If the application is listed, guide the user to install it from there.
2 Confirm approval. If the software is not in the catalogue, confirm the manager's approval and a licence cost centre. Send unapproved software to the security and procurement review process.
3 Check licence availability. Look in the licence tracker for free seats. If none are available, raise a procurement request and tell the user the expected timeline.
4 Install through the managed tool. Deploy through the endpoint management tool (for example Intune or SCCM) rather than a manual install, so it stays patched and inventoried.
5 Fix failures. For failed installs, check free disk space, pending restarts, administrator rights, and conflicts with older versions. Review the installer log and retry.
6 Assign and activate the licence. Assign the licence to the user's account and confirm activation. Remove the licence from users who have left or no longer need it.
7 Validate with the user. Confirm the application opens, the user can sign in, and any key files open correctly.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Software fails security review, or is on the prohibited list
Vendor-side licensing or activation errors
A rollout or update causes the same failure on many devices (possible major incident)

WI-05_Email_and_Calendar_Problems.pdf.title: WI-05 Email and Calendar Problems
WI-05_Email_and_Calendar_Problems.pdf.summary: Use this instruction for problems sending, receiving, or accessing email, and for calendar and mailbox configuration issues. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if a whole team or executive is affected) Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 2 business hours Handled by: Tier 1, then Tier 2 / messaging team Related: WI-10 Security Incidents, WI-11 Mobile Devices, WI-12 Video Conferencing

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Cannot send or receive messages, or messages stuck in Outbox
Outlook shows "Disconnected" or keeps asking for a password
Mailbox full, or shared mailbox missing
Meeting invites not appearing, or calendar not syncing

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Email address affected and any bounce-back (NDR) text
Whether the problem occurs in Outlook desktop, web, or mobile
Time of the last successful send or receive
Whether the issue affects one user, a group, or everyone

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Scope the problem. Check the service health dashboard first. If the platform is degraded, link the ticket to the major incident and update the user.
2 Test in webmail. Ask the user to sign in to Outlook on the web. If it works there, the fault is with the desktop client or profile. If it fails, the fault is with the account or mailbox.
3 Check the account and mailbox. Verify the licence, mailbox size and quota, sign-in status, and any mail flow rules, forwarding, or blocked-sender entries.
4 Fix the client. Restart Outlook in safe mode, clear cached credentials, run the Office repair, or create a new Outlook profile. Re-add the mailbox if it is a shared mailbox.

5 Read the bounce message. For delivery failures, read the NDR code. Common causes are a mistyped address, recipient mailbox full, message too large, or a blocked domain. Check the message trace for details.
6 Check for spam and quarantine. If messages are missing, check the junk folder and the admin quarantine. Release safe messages and add the sender to the allow list if approved.
7 Confirm resolution. Ask the user to send and receive a test message and check that the calendar shows correct meetings.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Suspected account compromise, unexpected forwarding rules, or phishing campaign (see WI-10)
Mail flow problems affecting multiple users or external delivery
Mailbox corruption, or a restore request for deleted items beyond retention

WI-06_Wi_Fi_and_Network_Connectivity.pdf.title: WI-06 Wi-Fi and Network Connectivity
WI-06_Wi_Fi_and_Network_Connectivity.pdf.summary: Use this instruction when a user cannot connect to the corporate network or the internet, or the connection is unstable or slow. Priority: P2 High if a site or floor is down, otherwise P3 Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 4 business hours Handled by: Tier 1, then Network team Related: WI-07 VPN, WI-16 Meeting Room AV, WI-10 Security Incidents

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: "No internet" or limited connectivity indicator
Cannot join the corporate Wi-Fi, or keeps disconnecting
Wired port is dead, or the dock does not give a connection
Websites or internal apps are slow or time out

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Location (building, floor, desk) and device hostname
Wi-Fi or wired, and the network name (SSID)
Whether other users nearby are affected
Result of a ping to the gateway and to an external site

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Scope the issue. Ask nearby users or check the monitoring dashboard. If many users are affected, treat it as an outage and escalate to the Network team at once.
2 Check the device. Confirm Wi-Fi is on and airplane mode is off. Toggle the adapter, then restart the device. Check that the IP address is valid and is not a 169.254.x.x address.

3 Test layer by layer. Ping the default gateway, then a public IP address, then a domain name. Failure at the gateway means local connection, at the public IP means routing or the firewall, and at the name means DNS.
4 Reset the connection. Forget and rejoin the Wi-Fi network, renew the IP lease, flush DNS, and reset the network stack. Update the network adapter driver if outdated.
5 Check the physical layer. For wired problems, swap the cable, try another wall port and another dock, and check the port in the switch management tool.
6 Try an alternative. Test on another known-good device or another network (for example a mobile hotspot, if policy allows) to see if the fault follows the user or the location.
7 Confirm stable connection. Verify access to the internet, an internal application, and a file share. Watch for a few minutes to confirm there are no drops.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Multiple users or a whole location affected
Faulty switch port, wireless access point, or cabling
Suspected unauthorized device or rogue access point on the network (see WI-10)

WI-07_VPN_and_Remote_Access.pdf.title: WI-07 VPN and Remote Access
WI-07_VPN_and_Remote_Access.pdf.summary: Use this instruction when a user working remotely cannot connect to the VPN or reach internal resources. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if many remote users affected) Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 2 business hours Handled by: Tier 1, then Tier 2 / Network Related: WI-06 Network, WI-10 Security Incidents, WI-01 Password Reset

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: VPN client fails to connect, or disconnects often
Connected to the VPN but cannot reach internal sites or file shares
Remote desktop session refused or very slow
Certificate or MFA errors at VPN sign-in

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Location and type of home network (home broadband, mobile hotspot, public Wi-Fi)
VPN client name and version, and the exact error text
Whether the user can reach the internet and cloud apps without the VPN
Time of the last successful connection

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Confirm internet access. Verify the user has a working internet connection without the VPN. Restart the home router if needed, and test on another network.
2 Check the account. Confirm the account is active, not locked, and in the VPN access group. Check MFA registration and look for failed sign-in attempts in the logs.
3 Check the VPN client. Confirm the client version is current and the profile is correct. Restart the client, then reinstall it if the fault continues.
4 Check the device. Confirm the date and time are correct, the device certificate is valid, and the device is compliant with security policy.
5 Rule out local blocks. Look for personal firewalls, third-party antivirus, or a router that blocks the VPN ports. Try another network to compare.
6 Fix access after connecting. If connected but unable to reach resources, flush DNS, check the assigned VPN IP and routes, and confirm the target service is reachable from the internal network.
7 Verify and document. Have the user open an internal application and a file share. Share the VPN quick guide and how to report slowness.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: VPN gateway or authentication service errors, or many users failing at once
Account shows sign-ins from unusual locations (see WI-10)
Access requested to a restricted network segment (needs approval)

WI-08_Printer_Scanner_and_Multifunction_.title: WI-08 Printer, Scanner and Multifunction Device Issues
WI-08_Printer_Scanner_and_Multifunction_.summary: Use this instruction for problems printing, scanning, or copying, and for adding or changing printers. Priority: P4 Low (P3 if the only printer for a team) Response target: Respond in 30 min / resolve in 4 business hours Handled by: Tier 1, then deskside / vendor Related: WI-06 Network, WI-03 Laptops and Peripherals, WI-18 Asset Management
topics: Printer, Scanner and Multifunction Device Issues

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Print job stuck in queue, or printer shows Offline
Printing garbled text, blank pages, or wrong paper size
Scan to email or scan to folder not working
User cannot find or add a printer

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Printer name, location, and asset or IP
Which users and which applications are affected
Error message on the printer panel or the computer
Whether the printer works from another computer

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the printer. Look at the panel for paper jams, empty paper or toner, open doors, and error codes. Power cycle the device if it is unresponsive.
2 Check the connection. Confirm the printer has a network link, and ping its IP address. Verify it shows online on the print server.
3 Clear the queue. Cancel stuck jobs, then restart the print spooler service on the user's computer or the print server.
4 Fix the driver or mapping. Remove and re-add the printer using the correct driver. Make sure the user is connected to the right queue, not an old or duplicate one.
5 Test from another device. If another user can print, the fault is on the first computer. If nobody can, the fault is with the printer or the server.
6 Fix scanning. For scan-to-email or folder, check the address book entry, the SMTP relay or service account password, and the permissions on the destination folder.
7 Print a test page. Have the user print a test page and a real document, and confirm the output quality.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Hardware faults (fuser, rollers, board) or repeated jams: log a service call with the vendor
Print server down or affecting many users
Request for a new printer or a move needs a change request

WI-09_Access_and_Permission_Requests.pdf.title: WI-09 Access and Permission Requests
WI-09_Access_and_Permission_Requests.pdf.summary: Use this instruction when a user asks for access to a folder, application, group, or system, or reports "Access denied". Priority: P4 Low (P3 if tied to a deadline) Response target: Respond in 30 min / fulfil in 1 business day after approval Handled by: Tier 1 / Tier 2 Related: WI-17 Offboarding, WI-02 Onboarding, WI-10 Security Incidents

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: "You do not have permission" when opening a file, site, or application
New role or project needs additional access
User needs to be added to or removed from a group or list

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Exact resource (path, URL, application, or group name)
Access level needed: read, edit, or admin
Business reason and the duration (permanent or temporary)
Requester's manager and the data owner

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Confirm the requester. Check that the request comes from the user or their manager through the ticket portal, and that the user is an active employee.
2 Identify the owner. Find the data or application owner in the access register. Access must be approved by the owner, not only by the user's manager.
3 Obtain approval. Send the approval request to the owner and record the approval in the ticket. Do not grant access on verbal approval alone.
4 Apply least privilege. Grant only the level requested, using a group where possible rather than direct assignment. Set an expiry date for temporary access.
5 Check for conflicts. For finance, HR, and other sensitive systems, check segregation-of-duties rules and escalate to the application owner if there is a conflict.
6 Confirm access. Ask the user to sign out and in again, then open the resource. Allow time for group membership changes to replicate.
7 Record the change. Note who approved, what was granted, and any expiry date, so the access can be reviewed later.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Requests for administrator or privileged rights
Owner cannot be identified or does not respond within the approval window
User claims to have lost access that was never recorded as granted

WI-10_Security_Incidents_Phishing_Malwar.title: WI-10 Security Incidents: Phishing, Malware and Lost Devices
WI-10_Security_Incidents_Phishing_Malwar.summary: Use this instruction when a user reports a suspicious email, a security warning, signs of compromise, or a lost or stolen device. Speed matters more than perfect documentation. Priority: P1 Critical / P2 High, depending on impact Response target: Respond in 5 to 15 min; contain immediately Handled by: Tier 1 triage, then Security team Related: WI-01 Password Reset, WI-05 Email and Calendar, WI-11 Mobile Devices
topics: Security Incidents: Phishing, Malware and Lost Devices

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: User clicked a link or opened an attachment in a suspicious email
Antivirus or endpoint alert on a device
Unexpected password change, MFA prompts the user did not trigger, or odd sent mail
Laptop, phone, or access badge lost or stolen

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: What happened, when, and what the user did (clicked, entered a password, downloaded a file)
Sender, subject, and the link or file (get the original message, not a screenshot)
Device, hostname, and location
Whether other users received the same message

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Stay calm and act fast. Thank the user for reporting. Tell them not to delete the message or restart the device unless told to, as this may remove evidence.
2 Raise the incident. Create a security incident ticket at P2 or higher and notify the Security team by the on-call process. Do not wait for the investigation to finish.
3 Contain the account. If credentials may be exposed, reset the password, revoke active sessions and tokens, and review MFA methods and mailbox forwarding rules.
4 Contain the device. For malware, isolate the device from the network through the endpoint security tool, or ask the user to disconnect from the network. Do not power off unless told to.

5 Handle lost or stolen devices. Lock or remotely wipe the device through device management, disable the account sessions, and record the loss time and location. The user should also report theft to the police if applicable.
6 Check for spread. Search for the same message across mailboxes and remove it. Block the sender, link, or file hash with the Security team.
7 Inform and record. Tell the user what has been done and what to expect. Record a clear timeline of actions in the ticket.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Always involve the Security team for confirmed compromise, data exposure, or ransomware
Multiple users affected or evidence of spread: declare a major incident
Possible personal data breach: notify the Data Protection Officer without delay

WI-11_Mobile_Devices_and_Mobile_Email.pd.title: WI-11 Mobile Devices and Mobile Email
WI-11_Mobile_Devices_and_Mobile_Email.pd.summary: Use this instruction for company-issued or approved personal mobile devices, including email setup, enrolment, app issues, and sync problems. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if the device is business critical) Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 4 business hours Handled by: Tier 1 / Tier 2 Related: WI-10 Security Incidents, WI-01 Password Reset, WI-05 Email and Calendar

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Work email, calendar, or contacts not syncing on the phone
Cannot enrol the device in device management
Company app missing or failing to open
New phone setup, or device is non-compliant and blocked

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Device make, model, and operating system version
Company-issued or personal device
Error message or screenshot
Whether the problem began after a phone update or a password change

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check eligibility. Confirm the device is on the supported list and the user has approval for mobile access. Personal devices must accept the mobile security policy.
2 Check basic settings. Confirm mobile data or Wi-Fi works, the operating system is up to date, and the device passcode meets policy.
3 Check compliance. Open the device management console. A device that is non-compliant (jailbroken, out of date, no passcode) will be blocked from corporate data until it is fixed.
4 Re-enrol or re-add the account. Remove the work account, restart the device, and add it again through the company portal and authenticator app. Update the saved password after any change.
5 Fix sync issues. Check that mail, calendar, and contacts sync is on and not paused by battery saver. Clear the app cache if needed.
6 Restore apps. Install company apps from the company portal. Confirm the app permissions and that the user is signed in with the correct account.
7 Confirm with the user. Have the user send a test email and open a company app. Remind them to report loss or theft right away (see WI-10).

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Device is lost or stolen (see WI-10)
Enrolment service errors affecting many users
Request to exempt a device from policy

WI-12_Video_Conferencing_and_Collaborati.title: WI-12 Video Conferencing and Collaboration Tools
WI-12_Video_Conferencing_and_Collaborati.summary: Use this instruction for problems joining or hosting online meetings, with audio or video devices, or with collaboration platforms such as Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if an executive meeting is about to start) Response target: Respond in 10 min / resolve in 1 business hour Handled by: Tier 1 Related: WI-16 Meeting Room AV, WI-06 Network, WI-03 Laptops and Peripherals

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Cannot join a meeting, or the link does not open
No sound, echo, or microphone not detected
Camera not working, or poor video quality
Screen sharing fails, or files will not sync or open

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Which platform and the meeting link or time
Whether the issue is audio, video, sharing, or sign-in
Headset, camera, and browser or app version
Whether others in the same meeting are affected

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the service status. Look at the platform status page. If there is a vendor outage, update the ticket, inform the user, and advise a backup channel such as a phone dial-in.
2 Check sign-in and version. Confirm the user is signed in with the work account and the app is on the current version. Restart the app or try the web version.

3 Check audio and video devices. In the app's device settings, select the correct microphone, speaker, and camera. Check the operating system privacy settings allow the app to use them, and that the device is not muted.
4 Test other connections. Close heavy apps, switch from Wi-Fi to wired, or leave the VPN if the platform allows. Check the user's bandwidth for slow video.

5 Fix sharing and permissions. For screen sharing, check the meeting policy and operating system screen-recording permissions. For file problems, check the sharing link and the user's permission on the site or folder.
6 Fix sync errors. For OneDrive or SharePoint sync issues, check the sync client status, free disk space, path length, and invalid file names. Reset the sync client if needed.
7 Test and confirm. Run a test call with the user, and confirm that the user can be heard, seen, and can share their screen.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Platform-wide outage, or a policy setting needs a change by the collaboration team
Meeting room equipment faults (raise with facilities or the AV team)
Data sharing concerns, such as files shared with the wrong people (see WI-10)

WI-13_Backup_File_Recovery_and_Restore_R.title: WI-13 Backup, File Recovery and Restore Requests
WI-13_Backup_File_Recovery_and_Restore_R.summary: Use this instruction when a user needs to recover a deleted, overwritten, or corrupted file, folder, or mailbox item, or when a system or server restore is requested. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if business-critical data is lost) Response target: Respond in 30 min / restore in 4 business hours Handled by: Tier 2, then Infrastructure Related: WI-10 Security Incidents, WI-09 Access Requests, WI-05 Email and Calendar
topics: Backup, File Recovery and Restore Requests

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: File or folder deleted by mistake
A document was saved over with the wrong content
File is corrupted and will not open
Mailbox items missing after a clean-up
A restore of a server or a database is requested

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Full path or location of the file, and its exact name
Date and time it was last known to be correct
How it was lost (deleted, overwritten, corrupted, ransomware suspected)
Who owns the data, and how urgent the need is

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the easy options first. Look in the Recycle Bin, the cloud storage recycle bin, and the Deleted Items or Recoverable Items folder. Most losses are recovered here without a restore.
2 Try version history. In OneDrive, SharePoint, or the file server's Previous Versions, open the history and restore the last good version. Confirm with the user before replacing the current file.
3 Confirm what is needed. If the data is not in these places, confirm the exact item, location, and point in time. A precise request saves time and avoids restoring the wrong data.
4 Get approval where required. Restores of shared or sensitive data need approval from the data owner. A restore of a system needs a change record and approval from the service owner.
5 Run the restore to a safe location. Restore to an alternative location first, never directly over the live data. Check the restored copy with the user before moving it back.
6 Check for wider problems. If many files have changed or been renamed at once, or extensions look unusual, stop and treat it as a possible ransomware event (see WI-10).
7 Confirm and record. Ask the user to open the file and confirm that the content is correct. Record the restore point, the source backup, and the time it took.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Backup job failed or the required restore point does not exist
Large restores, server restores, or database restores
Signs of ransomware, mass deletion, or malicious activity

WI-14_Business_Application_and_Line_of_B.title: WI-14 Business Application and Line-of-Business System Issues
WI-14_Business_Application_and_Line_of_B.summary: Use this instruction when a business application is not working, is slow, or gives errors, such as ERP, CRM, payroll, HR, or finance systems. The goal is to find out quickly whether the fault is local, the user's account, or the application itself. Priority: P2 High (P1 if a critical business process is stopped) Response target: Respond in 15 min / update hourly Handled by: Tier 1 triage, then Application support Related: WI-09 Access Requests, WI-20 Browser and Web Apps, WI-04 Software
topics: Business Application and Line-of-Business System Issues

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Error message on login or when saving a record
Application is slow or times out
A report or batch job fails
Data is missing or displays incorrectly
A page works for some users but not others

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Name of the application and the function being used
Exact error message, screenshot, and the time it occurred
Number of users affected and which departments
Whether it worked before, and any recent change or upgrade

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check for known issues. Look in the incident list and the status page for a known outage or planned maintenance. If one exists, link the ticket and give the user the update.
2 Establish the scope. Ask whether colleagues have the same problem. One user points to the account or device. Many users point to the application or infrastructure.
3 Reproduce the fault. Try the same steps on your own test account or the user's device with remote assistance. Note exactly where it fails.
4 Check the user's account. Verify the account is active and the user has the right role, licence, and permissions. Check for recent changes to roles.
5 Check the client side. Clear the browser cache, try another browser, test from another device, and check for required plug-ins or client updates.
6 Capture evidence for support. Record error text, timestamps, user IDs, transaction names, and screenshots. Include steps to reproduce. Good evidence shortens the fix time.
7 Escalate and keep the user informed. Pass the ticket to the application support team with the evidence. Agree on a workaround if there is one, and update the user at the agreed intervals.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Multiple users affected, or a critical process (payroll, month-end close, order entry) is blocked
Data appears wrong, lost, or exposed (raise a security and data incident)
The fault started right after a release or change

WI-15_Telephony_Desk_Phones_and_Softphon.title: WI-15 Telephony, Desk Phones and Softphone Issues
WI-15_Telephony_Desk_Phones_and_Softphon.summary: Use this instruction for problems with desk phones, softphones, voicemail, call forwarding, number changes, and calling headsets. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if a team or reception is without phones) Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 2 business hours Handled by: Tier 1, then Telephony team Related: WI-06 Network, WI-12 Video Conferencing, WI-18 Asset Management
topics: Telephony, Desk Phones and Softphone Issues

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Phone shows no dial tone or 'registering'
Calls drop, crackle, or have one-way audio
Voicemail not working or not delivering to email
Call forwarding or hunt group not working
Softphone cannot sign in

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: User, extension or number, and location
Desk phone model or softphone application
Whether inbound, outbound, or both are affected
Time of the failed calls, and the numbers involved

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check for a wider fault. See if other phones in the same area or building are affected, and check the telephony monitoring. If many are, escalate to the Telephony team at once.
2 Check power and connection. Confirm a desk phone has power (network port or adapter) and a network cable. Try another port or a known-good cable.
3 Restart the device. Power cycle the phone. For a softphone, sign out, close the app, and sign back in. Check the user's licence and extension assignment.
4 Check audio devices. For one-way audio or poor quality, check the headset, volume, and the audio device selected. Test with another headset.
5 Check network quality. Poor audio is often caused by network congestion or Wi-Fi. Test on a wired connection and check for VPN use, which can add delay.
6 Check call settings. Confirm call forwarding, do-not-disturb, hunt group membership, and voicemail settings in the telephony portal.
7 Make a test call. Place inbound and outbound calls with the user. Confirm voicemail and forwarding if relevant.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Many phones or a whole site affected, or calls to emergency numbers cannot be made
Contact centre queue or hunt group fault
Trunk, number porting, or carrier faults

WI-16_Meeting_Room_Display_and_Audio_Vis.title: WI-16 Meeting Room, Display and Audio-Visual Equipment
WI-16_Meeting_Room_Display_and_Audio_Vis.summary: Use this instruction for faults with meeting room equipment: displays, projectors, conferencing systems, microphones, speakers, cameras, touch panels, and wireless presentation. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if an executive or client meeting is within the hour) Response target: Respond in 10 min / on-site within 30 min for urgent Handled by: Tier 1, then deskside / AV team Related: WI-12 Video Conferencing, WI-15 Telephony, WI-06 Network
topics: Meeting Room, Display and Audio-Visual Equipment

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Room display shows no signal
Conferencing system will not start a meeting
No sound, echo, or feedback in the room
Laptop will not connect to the screen
Touch panel is frozen or shows an error

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Room name and building, and the meeting start time
Equipment affected and any messages on the screen
Whether the problem is with a laptop connection or the room system
Who is hosting, and whether the meeting has external guests

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Prioritize by meeting time. If a meeting is imminent, get a quick workaround ready first: join from a laptop and use the room display or a phone dial-in.
2 Check power and cables. Confirm the display, codec, and speakers are on and the right input is selected. Reseat HDMI, USB, and network cables.
3 Check the room system. Look at the touch panel and the room system status in the management portal. Restart the room system if it is offline.
4 Check the laptop connection. Try another cable or adapter, set display mode to extend or duplicate, and check the resolution. Try a second laptop to separate laptop and room faults.
5 Check audio. Check that microphones are not muted and that the right speaker and microphone are chosen. Reduce echo by lowering the volume or muting unused devices.
6 Check network and sign-in. Confirm the room account is signed in and that the system has a network connection. Check the calendar link if meetings do not appear.
7 Test and record. Run a short test call with the user. Record the fault and the fix on the room's equipment record.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Room system is offline and cannot be restored remotely
Hardware fault (display, camera, microphone, panel) that needs a vendor or AV engineer
Repeated faults in the same room, which may indicate a design or network issue

WI-17_Employee_Offboarding_and_Account_T.title: WI-17 Employee Offboarding and Account Termination
WI-17_Employee_Offboarding_and_Account_T.summary: Use this instruction when an employee, contractor, or intern leaves, moves roles, or needs urgent access removal. It protects company data and ensures licences and equipment are recovered. Priority: P3 Medium (P1 for urgent security terminations) Response target: Immediate for security cases / on the last working day otherwise Handled by: Tier 2, with Security and HR Related: WI-09 Access Requests, WI-02 Onboarding, WI-18 Asset Management

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: HR notice of a resignation or end of contract
Manager requests removal of access for a leaver
Urgent termination request from HR or Security
Access remains after someone changes teams

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Name, employee ID, last working day, and time of access removal
Whether the termination is standard, urgent, or sensitive
Manager and nominated person for mailbox and file handover
Equipment issued and any pending returns

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Confirm the request. Accept offboarding requests only from HR or the line manager through the approved process. Confirm the dates and whether this is an urgent security removal.
2 Time the access removal. For standard exits, schedule account disablement for the end of the last working day. For urgent cases, disable immediately and revoke active sessions.
3 Disable and secure the account. Disable sign-in, reset the password, revoke sessions and tokens, remove MFA methods, and remove the user from groups and distribution lists.

4 Handle mailbox and files. Set an out-of-office or forwarding to the manager as approved. Convert to a shared mailbox or apply retention as per policy. Transfer file ownership and cloud storage content to the manager.
5 Recover equipment. Arrange the return of the laptop, phone, tokens, and badge. Record the asset tags, wipe devices after data has been secured, and update the register.
6 Remove licences and external access. Remove software licences, application accounts, VPN access, and any third-party access. Check shared accounts and update shared passwords the person knew.
7 Confirm and record. Verify the account is disabled and has no active sessions. Attach the completed checklist and the approvals, and set the deletion date according to the retention policy.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Termination involves a dispute, investigation, or legal hold (involve HR, Legal, and Security)
Evidence of data copying or unusual activity before departure
Equipment is not returned, or a device is lost

WI-18_Hardware_Requests_Asset_Management.title: WI-18 Hardware Requests, Asset Management and Returns
WI-18_Hardware_Requests_Asset_Management.summary: Use this instruction for requests for new or replacement hardware, loaner devices, accessories, asset moves, returns, and disposal. Accurate asset records are the basis for security, support, and audit. Priority: P4 Low (P3 if the user has no working device) Response target: Respond in 30 min / fulfil in 3 business days Handled by: Tier 2 / Asset team Related: WI-03 Laptops and Peripherals, WI-02 Onboarding, WI-17 Offboarding
topics: Hardware Requests, Asset Management and Returns

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: User needs a new laptop, monitor, phone, or accessory
Device is due for replacement or beyond repair
Equipment is moving between users or locations
Device returned by a leaver or an unused device found
Asset record does not match the device in use

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: User, department, cost centre, and manager approval
Equipment needed, quantity, and business reason
Required date, and location for delivery
Asset tag, serial number, and current user for replacements and returns

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the standard. Compare the request with the hardware standard for the role. Standard items can be approved by the manager. Non-standard items need further approval and a business case.
2 Check stock and warranty. Look in stock for suitable equipment before ordering. For a replacement, check the warranty status and whether a repair is possible.
3 Get approvals and raise the order. Attach the manager's approval and the cost centre. Raise a purchase request if stock is not available, and tell the user the expected delivery time.
4 Prepare the equipment. Image and enrol the device, install the standard software, apply encryption and security policies, and label it with the asset tag.
5 Deliver and hand over. Hand the device to the user, check their identity, and record the handover. Show them how to sign in and where to get help. Get a signature or an electronic acknowledgement.
6 Update the asset register. Record the serial number, asset tag, user, location, status, and purchase and warranty dates. Mark old devices as returned or pending disposal.

7 Process returns and disposal. Collect old equipment, back up data if needed, securely wipe the drive, and record the wipe. Dispose of or recycle through the approved supplier and keep the certificate.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Request exceeds the budget or the hardware standard
Equipment is lost, stolen, or not returned (see WI-10)
Stock levels are too low to meet demand

WI-19_Operating_System_Updates_Patching_.title: WI-19 Operating System Updates, Patching and Restart Issues
WI-19_Operating_System_Updates_Patching_.summary: Use this instruction when a device fails to install updates, restarts unexpectedly, is flagged non-compliant for missing patches, or has problems after an update. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if many devices are affected) Response target: Respond in 30 min / resolve in 4 business hours Handled by: Tier 2, then Endpoint team Related: WI-03 Laptops and Peripherals, WI-04 Software, WI-10 Security Incidents
topics: Operating System Updates, Patching and Restart Issues

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Update stuck or fails with an error code
Device keeps asking to restart
Device flagged as non-compliant for missing updates
Problems started right after an update
Update takes too long or uses too much bandwidth

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: Hostname, operating system version, and build number
Update name or KB number, and the error code
When the update started, and how long the device has been up
Whether other devices have the same issue

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the scope. Check the update management console. If many devices fail the same update, treat it as a possible bad release, stop the rollout, and escalate to the Endpoint team.
2 Check the basics. Check free disk space (at least 15 GB is a good minimum), battery or power, and the network connection. Restart the device to complete any pending update.
3 Review the error. Look at the update history and the error code. Search the knowledge base and the vendor documentation for the code.
4 Run the built-in troubleshooter. Run the update troubleshooter, reset the update components, and check the system file integrity. Retry the installation.
5 Clear a blocked update. Check for third-party security tools, VPN, or proxy that block the update. Install the update manually from the update catalogue if needed.
6 Roll back if necessary. If the device is unstable after an update, uninstall the update or restore from a restore point. Pause the update on that device and report to the Endpoint team.
7 Confirm compliance. Check the device reports as compliant in the console. Tell the user when to restart and how to schedule restarts outside working time.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Many devices fail the same update
Update causes data loss, boot failure, or business application faults
Critical security patches cannot be installed within the required timeframe

WI-20_Web_Browser_Intranet_and_Web_Appli.title: WI-20 Web Browser, Intranet and Web Application Problems
WI-20_Web_Browser_Intranet_and_Web_Appli.summary: Use this instruction when a user cannot open or use a website, an intranet page, or a web application in the browser, or sees certificate, sign-in, or loading errors. Priority: P3 Medium (P2 if a company-wide web service is affected) Response target: Respond in 15 min / resolve in 2 business hours Handled by: Tier 1, then Tier 2 / Web team Related: WI-10 Security Incidents, WI-06 Network, WI-14 Business Applications
topics: Web Browser, Intranet and Web Application Problems

sections.heading: Common symptoms
items: Page will not load or times out
Certificate or 'connection is not private' warning
Endless sign-in loop with single sign-on
Page layout broken or buttons do nothing
A site is blocked by the web filter

sections.heading: Information to collect
items: The full address (URL) and the exact error message
Browser and version, and whether other browsers show the same
Whether it works on another device, network, or for another user
When it last worked, and any recent change

sections.heading: Resolution steps
items: 1 Check the service. Test the site from your own device and check the status page. If the site is down for everyone, link to the incident and update the user.
2 Test another browser. Try the site in a second browser and in a private window. This separates a browser fault from an account or site fault.
3 Clear cache and cookies. Clear the cached files and cookies for the site, restart the browser, and try again. Disable extensions and test.

4 Check date, time and certificate. Check the device date and time are right, and read the certificate warning. A wrong clock or an untrusted certificate is a common cause. Do not tell users to bypass real warnings.
5 Check sign-in and policies. For sign-in loops, clear cookies, check the account and MFA status, and test with another browser profile. Check for conflicting accounts signed in at the same time.

6 Check the web filter and network. If the site is blocked, check the category and the business need. Request an unblock through the approved process rather than disabling the filter. Test on another network.
7 Update or reset the browser. Update the browser to the current version, reset it to defaults if needed, and confirm that the user's bookmarks and passwords are synced first.

sections.heading: Escalate when
items: Certificate errors on internal or company sites affecting many users
Suspected malicious site, redirect, or browser hijack (see WI-10)
Web filter change requests that need Security approval
